extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in computer vision, image/video processing, and computational pathology (histopathology virtual staining)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating algorithms for virtual staining of histopathology images, especially unpaired multi-domain image translation that preserves diagnostic structure while transferring staining style. Focus is on methods using prompt learning and inversion strategies to disentangle content and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintaining strict structural consistency is crucial, as histopathology images emphasize structural integrity more than natural images. Even slight structural alterations can lead to deviations in diagnostic semantic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design methods that avoid altering tissue structure during style transfer. In this work, the Structural Target path (inversion of the input image) and visual prompt images are used to maintain structural consistency. Evaluate algorithms for minimal structural distortion because changes can affect diagnosis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of pathological diagnostic content
rubrics_metrics.description: Preserve complete pathological diagnostic content despite unpaired training data which may compromise diagnostic information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Techniques should explicitly safeguard diagnostic features (cells, tissue morphology) across staining transformations. The proposed dual-path inversion aims to retain complete pathological diagnostic content by separating structural and style targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate style transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce accurate style transfer results that match the target staining appearance (coloration, texture) while not corrupting diagnostic content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a Style Target path (feature adapter generated reference/style templates) to guide style transfer. Quantitatively and qualitatively assess how well the target staining style is reproduced without harming structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete content-style disentanglement
rubrics_metrics.description: Achieve complete content-style disentanglement so content (structure) and style (stain appearance) are controlled independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement mechanisms (here: plug-and-play embedding visual prompt approach during deterministic sampling) that separate content and style representations, allowing control over each without leakage. Verify disentanglement empirically (ablation, visualizations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual Path Prompted Strategy (structural and style targets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a dual-path approach: a Style Target path that provides style templates via a feature adapter, and a Structural Target path that is the inversion of the input image, with visual prompts maintaining structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Architectures should explicitly implement separate paths for style guidance and structural preservation. The feature adapter generates reference images for inversion; the visual prompt maintains structural consistency during inversion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize null visual prompt instead of fine-tuning
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize only the null visual prompt as an 'operator' for dual path inversion rather than fine-tuning the pre-trained model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor prompt optimization (lightweight parameter updates) to adapt models to staining tasks, reducing need to retrain or fine-tune large pre-trained networks. This supports efficiency and reuse of pre-trained weights.

rubrics_metrics.name: StainPrompt Optimization around pivotal noise timesteps
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize null visual prompt for structural and style trajectory around pivotal noise on each timestep to ensure accurate dual-path inversion reconstruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design prompt optimization to consider timestep-wise noise dynamics in diffusion/inversion processes; optimize prompts to guide both style and structural trajectories during denoising for faithful reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deterministic sampling for reliable inversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Use deterministic sampling processes to achieve consistent content-style disentanglement during inversion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ deterministic sampling schemes when reconstructing/inverting images so that prompts reliably control content and style; assess stability/repeatability of outputs across runs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robustness and generalization on unpaired multi-domain datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate high structural consistency and accurate style transfer across publicly available multi-domain unpaired staining datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate methods extensively on diverse unpaired datasets to show generalization across domains and staining types. Provide quantitative metrics and qualitative examples showing consistent performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation via extensive experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide extensive evaluations to demonstrate claims (high structural consistency, accurate style transfer).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report experimental results on public datasets, include comparisons/ablation studies to validate components (dual path, prompt optimization, deterministic sampling), and present metrics and visual examples that substantiate preservation of diagnostic content and style fidelity.
